title: Probe localization — 9q34
clinical_history: Place the ABL1 FISH probe on the chromosome 9 map. Band numbering follows the same ordered segments used in chromosome assembly. Demonstration ideogram.

probe_type_expected.detects: presence, copy number, or partner of a specific locus
probe_type_expected.normal_pattern: two red signals on the two chromosomes 9

hints: 9q34 is on the long arm of chromosome 9, distal (toward qter).
Numbering increases from the centromere toward the telomere, so q34 is farther from cen than q21.
A locus-specific probe marks a band; a centromeric probe marks copy number of a whole chromosome.
explanation: The probe object stores chromosome 9, arm q, and band 34, matching segment 9q34 in chromosome-maps.json. FISH localization reuses that map rather than a separate drawing.
plain_language_interpretation: The red probe belongs at 9q34 on the chromosome 9 ideogram.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020. Basel: Karger; 2020. Band designation.
